name: Tether
thesis: One custom TypeScript daemon on the laptop is the single source of truth for everything running there; the phone is a thin Expo client that assumes it is always disconnected and catches up from cursors. Agents are driven only through structured protocols (Claude Agent SDK natively, ACP for everyone else) — never by scraping TUIs (Omnara's deprecation is the cautionary tale) — while tmux is the one capture layer for raw terminals. Transport is Tailscale-direct with zero public endpoints and typed operations only, because this is remote command execution on a personal machine.
laptop_side: A single Node/TypeScript daemon, `tetherd`, installed as a launchd LaunchAgent (must run as the logged-in user or it lands on the wrong tmux socket — terminal research pitfall). Components inside one process: (1) Fastify HTTP + WebSocket server bound exclusively to the laptop's Tailscale 100.x address, fronted by `tailscale serve` for real Let's Encrypt TLS on the ts.net MagicDNS name with automatic cert renewal (raw `tailscale cert` files expire in 90 days unrenewed — transport research). (2) Agent adapter tier 1: Claude via @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk `query()` with `includePartialMessages` for streaming, `canUseTool` for the approvals inbox, and the `PermissionRequest` hook to trigger push (the SDK docs explicitly recommend this hook for external notifications). Built on `query()` + options only — the V2 createSession API was removed in 0.3.142. (3) Agent adapter tier 2: an ACP client on @agentclientprotocol/sdk spawning Gemini CLI (`--experimental-acp`) and Codex via @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp as stdio subprocesses; the daemon implements ACP's client-side terminal capability so agents' shell commands stream live. Never `codex exec` — it has zero approval prompts. (4) Terminal adapter: one long-lived `tmux -C attach` control-mode client on the default per-user socket (hosted under node-pty); %output notifications octal-decoded to raw bytes, `capture-pane -p -e -S -` for scrollback replay on phone connect, `send-keys` for input, pause-mode flow control (`refresh-client -f pause-after=...`) so a `yarn build` cannot flood LTE. (5) Persistence: better-sqlite3 holding a cursor-addressed append-only event log per session (the reconnect-replay backbone, with includePartialMessages deltas batched before writing), approvals table with expiry, hashed per-device auth tokens, and an audit log of every mutating call. Plus the daemon's own transcript mirror for ACP agents, because ACP session/load cold-recovery is unreliable in practice. (6) Push dispatcher: expo-server-sdk → Expo Push Service, content-free payloads. (7) A thin optional VS Code companion extension (separate install, Phase 4) that connects OUT to the daemon over localhost WebSocket as a sensor/actuator only — the daemon owns everything that must survive VS Code closing.
phone_side: Expo (React Native + TypeScript) app with expo-dev-client from day one — Expo Go cannot receive remote push, and a PWA is disqualified because iOS web push has no action buttons and materially worse delivery than APNs (phone research). Distribution: paid Apple Developer Program ($99/yr, non-negotiable for the push entitlement) + TestFlight internal testing on iOS (90-day re-upload cadence, CI-reminded); EAS-built APK sideload on Android, registering the free 20-device limited-distribution account before the Sept 2026 verification enforcement. App structure: three tabs — Inbox (approvals + AskUserQuestion cards, badge-counted), Sessions (grouped: agents / terminals / IDE, each labeled with capture fidelity), Activity (audit feed). Session detail renders agent streams as a FlashList of parsed message blocks (cheap, selectable, chat-like — not xterm), with an xterm.js-in-WebView view (pattern: @fressh/react-native-xtermjs-webview, rAF + 8KB write coalescing) reserved for real PTY sessions, rendered at the pane's laptop-side size with pan/pinch — the phone NEVER resizes the PTY, since Claude Code's ink TUI demonstrably corrupts on resize. Custom accessory key row for Esc/Ctrl/Tab/arrows. expo-notifications category "approval" with Approve + Deny actions (Deny carries a text-input for a steering reply), interruption-level time-sensitive, `opensAppToForeground:false`. Device token and pairing credential in expo-secure-store behind Face ID. Networking: one WebSocket while foregrounded, torn down on background (iOS suspends within seconds and background URLSession has no WebSocket support), every stream resumed by cursor on foreground — the app never assumes the socket survived.
transport: Tailscale-direct, no relay. Laptop + phone on the free Personal plan (well within 6 users / unlimited devices); daemon bound only to the tailnet interface so home-Wi-Fi devices cannot even reach the port; HTTPS/WSS via `tailscale serve` on `laptop.<tailnet>.ts.net` — real TLS, so no iOS ATS exceptions. iOS VPN On Demand with the *.ts.net hostname trigger (interface rule set to "Do Nothing", the documented requirement) auto-raises the tunnel when the app dials the MagicDNS name; no Tailscale SDK embedding needed since the tunnel is device-wide. Battery is fine because the laptop is never an exit node. Day-one setup: disable Tailscale key expiry on the laptop node (180-day default silently kills it) and pmset to prevent sleep while plugged in. On top of WireGuard: app-level auth via QR pairing on the laptop that hands the phone a per-device random bearer token, stored hashed on the daemon, individually revocable, shown in a device list. The API is typed operations only — approveDecision(approvalId), sendMessage(sessionId), sendKeys(terminalId), startSession(agent, dir ∈ allowlisted roots), attachTerminal(id) — never a generic exec endpoint; terminal attach gets a separate per-session confirmation and all input is audit-logged. Why over Cloudflare Tunnel: Cloudflare's edge reads the plaintext command channel and a baked-in service token is a static bearer credential; why over a self-hosted relay: no internet-facing service to patch, and WireGuard gives device-to-device E2E for free (Happy shipped 'E2E' marketing while server-decryptable API keys sat in its relay — Discussion #680).
surface_capture: Four surfaces, each captured at the highest fidelity actually possible, labeled honestly in the UI. (1) CLAUDE CODE: hosted inside the daemon via Agent SDK `query()` — full structure: canUseTool approvals, includePartialMessages streaming, cwd pinned per session (resume from a different cwd silently forks a fresh session). Because SDK and CLI share ~/.claude/projects, phone-started sessions are resumable at the desk with `claude --resume <id>`; attach is treated as exclusive single-writer — the daemon releases via the defer hook decision before handoff (concurrent dual-writer behavior is UNVERIFIED). Sessions the user runs interactively in a tmux-wrapped terminal appear as terminal mirrors (screen-exact, no structured approvals); sessions inside the VS Code Claude chat panel are invisible — webview isolation makes that a hard wall, and the UI says so rather than pretending. (2) OTHER AI AGENTS: the ACP tier — Gemini CLI natively, Codex via the official codex-acp adapter; session/request_permission's four option kinds and session/update's tool-call lifecycle map 1:1 onto the same inbox and stream model, so every future ACP agent is free. Capabilities (loadSession, resume) are feature-detected at initialize; the daemon's own SQLite transcript mirror covers cold restarts. (3) PLAIN TERMINALS: tmux is the sole real capture layer. Setup installs tmux (not currently on the machine — brew prerequisite), sets history-limit before any session spawns, and switches VS Code's default terminal profile to `tmux new -A -s vscode-N` — after that, every new integrated or Terminal.app shell is fully mirrored (control-mode clients don't affect window sizing, so the phone watches without shrinking the laptop view) and gains crash persistence for free. The daemon can attach to ANY session on the user's tmux socket regardless of who launched tmux. Non-tmux terminals cannot be retro-attached (no macOS API for another process's PTY master; reptyr is Linux-only) — listed as "not capturable" or, in VS Code, downgraded per (4). (4) VS CODE ITSELF: the thin companion extension reports IDE state over stable APIs — workspaceFolders, activeTextEditor, tabGroups, window focus, terminal list with shell type/PID/cwd — and does best-effort mirroring of non-tmux integrated terminals via the shell-integration API (subscribe in onDidStartTerminalShellExecution, call execution.read() immediately; command-scoped, attach-at-start-only) with input via Terminal.sendText(shouldExecute=false) for raw keys. It never builds on onDidWriteTerminalData (forever-proposed, Marketplace-blocked) and never touches the Claude chat webview. Multiple VS Code windows mean multiple extension connections; the daemon namespaces them.
approvals_flow: Agent requests a non-auto-approved tool → the Claude SDK's canUseTool promise pends (or ACP sends session/request_permission) → daemon writes an approval row (id, session, tool name, input summary, diff payload, expiry) to SQLite, appends an event to the session's cursor stream, and the PermissionRequest hook fires the push dispatcher → Expo Push → APNs/FCM as a time-sensitive notification in the "approval" category, payload carrying only IDs (nothing sensitive transits Expo/Apple; 4KB cap is irrelevant). On the phone: lock-screen Approve/Deny buttons handle without opening the app (opensAppToForeground:false) and POST an idempotent, approval-ID-scoped decision over the tunnel; tapping the body deep-links into the inbox card, which fetches the full tool input/diff from the daemon — the guaranteed fallback, since killed-state action taps are the least reliable path on both platforms. "Always allow" maps to updatedPermissions (Claude) / allow_always (ACP); Deny's text-input doubles as a steering message queued to the session. The decision resolves the pending canUseTool promise ({behavior:'allow'|'deny'}) → the agent resumes → stream events flow to any connected client, and the desk view and phone stay in sync because both read the same event log. Robustness: decisions are idempotent with server-side expiry and a confirming state change in the inbox; unanswered approvals re-notify on an escalating schedule (push receipts only confirm handoff to APNs, not delivery); if the daemon must restart with an approval pending, it uses the SDK's defer hook decision and resumes the session rather than losing the prompt. Note the honest gap: canUseTool never fires for auto-approved tools, so a PreToolUse hook feeds those into the Activity feed instead of silently vanishing.
notifications: Laptop daemon → HTTPS POST to Expo Push Service (free, no public endpoint needed on the laptop, median 42ms handoff) → APNs/FCM. Event types: approval needed, AskUserQuestion, session finished, session errored, session idle-waiting, terminal bell (opt-in). All payloads content-free (IDs + generic titles); the app treats every push as a signal and fetches authoritative state on open. iOS uses time-sensitive interruption level (self-service capability, breaks through Focus) with graceful degradation if the user disables it; Android action buttons are tested on-device in week one given their history of killed-state no-ops (fixed in expo PR #35295 but reports continued). DeviceNotRegistered receipts rotate stored tokens; Expo push-security access tokens are enabled and the ExponentPushToken is treated as a secret. Because tickets/receipts never prove device delivery, the in-app inbox remains the source of truth and the daemon escalates unanswered approvals. Silent content-available pushes are never used for sync — foreground catch-up plus visible pushes only.
remote_start: New Task screen on the phone → project picker fed by the daemon from a configured allowlist of project roots (directories outside the allowlist cannot be targeted, by API shape not by validation) → choose agent (Claude / Gemini / Codex), initial prompt, and permission mode → typed startSession call. The daemon spawns: Claude via SDK query() with cwd pinned to the chosen directory (avoiding the cwd-keyed resume trap); ACP agents via session/new on a fresh subprocess; a plain terminal via `tmux new-session -d -c <dir>`, instantly mirrored. The session appears in the Sessions list streaming within seconds, the start is audit-logged, and a finish/needs-input push closes the loop. Claude sessions started this way are later resumable at the laptop with `claude --resume <id>` because SDK and CLI share the on-disk session store — remote start is not a one-way street.

build_phases.scope: Daemon skeleton: Fastify + WS on the Tailscale interface, tailscale serve TLS, SQLite event log with cursor replay, QR pairing with hashed per-device tokens, audit log. Claude tier only: Agent SDK sessions, canUseTool approvals, streaming, remote start in allowlisted dirs. Expo dev-client app: Sessions list, approval inbox, session detail as FlashList stream, New Task screen. Expo Push with Approve/Deny lock-screen actions, time-sensitive, killed-state testing on real devices. TestFlight + EAS Android build. Setup script: Tailscale key-expiry off, pmset, LaunchAgent install.
build_phases.deliverable: Leave the house while a Claude session runs: get a lock-screen push when it needs approval, approve/deny/steer from the phone, watch live output, and kick off new Claude tasks in any allowlisted project remotely. Complete daily-driver for the single biggest pain.

build_phases.scope: tmux control-mode adapter in the daemon (%output decode, capture-pane replay, send-keys, pause-mode flow control), setup step that installs tmux and switches the VS Code default terminal profile to the tmux wrapper, xterm.js-in-WebView terminal screen with write coalescing, pan/zoom at laptop-side pane size, custom Esc/Ctrl/arrow key row, per-session attach confirmation.
build_phases.deliverable: Every tmux-wrapped terminal (all new VS Code terminals post-setup, plus anything started with tmux) is watchable and typeable from the phone with instant scrollback replay — including interactive TUI agents run manually, mirrored screen-exact.

build_phases.scope: ACP client on @agentclientprotocol/sdk with capability feature-detection, Gemini CLI (--experimental-acp) and Codex (codex-acp) adapters, normalization of session/request_permission and session/update into the existing event schema, daemon-side transcript mirror for ACP sessions, client-side ACP terminal capability, agent picker in New Task.
build_phases.deliverable: Gemini and Codex sessions appear in the same Sessions list with the same approvals inbox, push actions, streaming, and remote start as Claude — one inbox for every agent.

build_phases.scope: Thin companion extension: IDE state reporting (workspace, editors, tabs, focus, terminal inventory with shell/cwd), best-effort shell-integration mirroring of non-tmux terminals with honest capability labels, sendText input routing with terminal-identity verification, multi-window namespacing. App polish: device management/revocation screen, escalating re-notify, Activity feed from PreToolUse hooks, desk-handoff button (defer + release for claude --resume).
build_phases.deliverable: The phone shows what the IDE is doing (open project, active file, every terminal and its state) and covers non-tmux terminals as far as the platform allows; token revocation and audit review are one tap; a phone session hands off cleanly to the desk CLI.

risks: Concurrent resume of the same Claude session by CLI and daemon is UNVERIFIED — the design assumes single-writer JSONL and enforces exclusive attach with defer-based handoff; if the assumption is wrong in a subtle way, transcript corruption is possible.

Sessions run inside the VS Code Claude chat panel are permanently invisible (webview isolation, no exported API verified) — the product mitigates by making daemon/CLI-in-tmux the steered default, but a user who lives in the chat panel gets nothing.

Killed-state notification action taps are the least reliable path on both platforms (Android no-op history, iOS background-JS edge cases); mitigated by idempotent decisions, expiry, escalating re-notify, and tap-to-open fallback — but 'approve from lock screen' will occasionally degrade to 'open the app'.

Anthropic SDK churn: the V2 session API was already removed once (0.3.142); canUseTool/hook semantics could shift under a personal-subscription auth model, and Agent SDK usage against a Claude subscription vs API billing is a cost/ToS detail to verify before Phase 1.

ACP maturity: Gemini/Codex adapter quality and optional capabilities vary; cold-restart recovery is community-reported weak, so the daemon's own transcript mirror is load-bearing, and Codex adapter behavior may lag Codex releases.

Ops fragility of a home server: laptop sleep, Tailscale key expiry, TestFlight 90-day build expiry, and tailscale-serve cert renewal are four independent ways the system dies silently while traveling — setup automation and a daemon self-health push reduce but don't eliminate this.

Shell-integration mirroring silently fails on nonstandard zsh configs (powerlevel10k instant prompt is a known offender) and is attach-at-start-only — Phase 4's non-tmux coverage is genuinely best-effort.
tmux wrapper only covers terminals opened after setup; pre-existing shells and deliberate non-tmux terminals stay dark, which the UI must keep saying honestly.
Expo Push is a third-party dependency in the critical alert path (metadata-only exposure, but availability matters); an outage means delayed approvals with no self-hosted fallback built.

Recurring costs/chores are structural: $99/yr Apple, Android developer-verification signup when enforcement reaches the region, and solo maintenance of three artifacts (daemon, app, extension) against moving targets — the Omnara lesson is why every agent integration sits on structured protocols, not TUI scraping.
not_built: No relay server or hosted backend — Tailscale WireGuard direct replaces the entire Happy-style relay + E2E-crypto layer (and its Discussion-#680 class of key-custody bugs).
No custom push infrastructure — Expo Push Service fronts APNs/FCM; payloads are content-free so nothing sensitive is entrusted to it.
No terminal emulator or multiplexer — xterm.js/@xterm/headless and tmux are adopted wholesale; ttyd/GoTTY/upterm/VibeTunnel are studied for architecture but not used as components.
No TUI scraping or PTY wrapping of agents — approvals and streaming come only from Agent SDK and ACP structured channels; the tmux mirror is a dumb screen, never parsed.
No Claude chat-panel integration and no onDidWriteTerminalData dependency — both are platform dead ends; at most the extension focuses the panel.
No codex exec path (zero approval prompts) and no ACP-only architecture (Claude gets the richer native SDK).
No generic shell-exec API endpoint — typed operations only; the security boundary is API shape.
No App Store / Play Store release, no multi-user accounts, no web client, no voice — one user, TestFlight + sideload.
No full-IDE-on-phone feature — 'code tunnel' to vscode.dev is documented as an escape hatch, not productized.
No custom session persistence for Claude — the shared ~/.claude/projects store is the database of record for transcripts; SQLite only holds events, approvals, auth, and ACP mirrors.
